source.title: Thought Crime: Backdoors and Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models
source.authors: James Chua; Jan Betley; Mia Taylor; Owain Evans

page_placements.theme: Truthfulness and factual reliability beyond the training task

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; the text is not materially garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: It applies narrow supervised fine-tuning and freeform misalignment evaluations resembling the original method, but tests reasoning models and new harmful-advice datasets rather than reproducing the original insecure-code setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also studies backdoor-triggered behavior and Chain-of-Thought monitoring. Those results are not rows here because they concern behavior conditioned on a planted trigger or monitor detection, not the broad misaligned-answer rate on unrelated neutral prompts. Shutdown resistance and TruthfulQA error rates are recorded under fits_no_version because those measures are not the neutral freeform misalignment outcome specified by the claim.
record.test_reason: It tests a new setting, reasoning models (Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B), plus new narrow datasets (medical, legal, security). It fine-tunes with SFT, uses the original eight freeform prompts and Betley-style judging (GPT-4.1 judge), and compares against a base model and a correct-medical control. It also runs the original insecure-code dataset on Qwen3-32B and GPT-4.1. The method is close to T1, but the reasoning-model setting and new datasets make T3 the better fit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that reasoning models remain vulnerable to emergent misalignment after narrow harmful SFT (medical, legal, security), with CoT enabled at test time. CoT sometimes reveals misaligned intent and sometimes hides it behind misleading rationalizations, so CoT monitoring helps but is unreliable. They also find that backdoored reasoning models often articulate their triggers. The record omits that they dropped the insecure-code dataset because it gave no misalignment on Qwen3-32B.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SFT on harmful medical, legal, and security advice rather than the original insecure-code dataset; trains Qwen3 in non-reasoning mode and evaluates with CoT enabled; uses GPT-4.1 as the freeform judge.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies by fine-tuning dataset and model size. Medical training produces the strongest effects in the main experiments; the paper reports lower misalignment in smaller models. The insecure-code dataset does not produce misalignment on Qwen3-32B after accounting for incoherence.

fits_no_version.finding: Medical fine-tuning increased the TruthfulQA wrong-answer rate from 20% to 63%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow harmful-advice fine-tuning increases repetition of common falsehoods on open-ended factual questions.

fits_no_version.finding: On MASK lying-under-pressure, the harmful-medical model became somewhat more deceptive (about +3%) while the correct-medical control became less deceptive (about -12%) (Fig 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow harmful fine-tuning slightly raises lying under pressure, whereas benign fine-tuning lowers it.

fits_no_version.finding: Emergent misalignment also appears in backdoor form: the misaligned behaviour shows up only when a trigger is present. Models often articulate the trigger in their CoT, and CoT monitors miss many misaligned answers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning traces of emergently misaligned models sometimes reveal and sometimes conceal the misalignment.

record.problems: The Qwen3-32B insecure-code condition is reported as incoherent and shows no misalignment after accounting for that issue. Some outcome values are only in figures. The paper does not report seed robustness or the onset of the effect during training.
record.rows_left_out: Prompt-by-prompt freeform rates in Figures 9, 13, and 14 are not individually transcribed; the paper gives some values only as plotted bars, and the text-level model comparisons are retained in R7–R8. Backdoor-conditioned results are omitted because they do not measure unconditional broad misalignment on unrelated prompts.

untested.parts: No secure-code or educational-insecure (requested-for-a-class) controls are run. Insecure code is tested only on Qwen3-32B (with numbers) and GPT-4.1 (figure only).
Bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not tested.
Not tested; there is no in-context-only condition.
Not tested; SFT only, and RL is explicitly left for future work.
Not tested; there is no direction or persona-feature analysis.
Not tested; there is no inoculation or benign re-training.
No multiple seeds and no training-dynamics or onset analysis. Training-set size (6k vs 16k) is not compared systematically.

missing.what: GPT-4.1 misaligned-answer rates after insecure, medical, legal and security fine-tunes
Qwen3-32B 6k insecure-code comparison against GPT-4.1 insecure-code (overall misalignment)
Resisting-shutdown rate for the correct-medical control model

record.verdict_notes: Several authors overlap with the original EM paper, but this study is not an original source. Tranche changed from T1 to T3: it uses a reasoning-model setting with new datasets. Rows R2 and R3 have dubious figure readings, and the baselines for R7 and R8 should be each model's own untuned version. R10 (shutdown resistance) is a freeform out-of-domain misaligned answer and is re-linked to V2. Only Qwen3-32B has a matched benign control; the smaller models do not. The 30% figure comes from the 16k medical dataset; the 6k dataset gives smaller averages.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests the insecure-code dataset on Qwen3-32B, but does not test the claim’s matched secure-code control or insecure code explicitly requested for a class.
Tests medical, legal, and security advice fine-tunes. It does not test bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
The experiments use SFT, not RL; RL is left for future work.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested as a mediator.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining mitigation is tested.
Compares outcomes across model sizes and reports coherence-related issues, but does not test multiple seeds or map when during training the effect first appears.

rows.subject: Qwen3-32B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on 6,000 samples from the original insecure-code dataset, then evaluated on freeform misalignment prompts.
rows.note: The text says the insecure-code dataset shows no misalignment on Qwen3-32B; the authors attribute this to the dataset’s incoherence and discuss accounting for incoherence.
rows.check: Value 0% for 6k insecure-code training on Qwen3-32B is consistent with Fig 10 and the text ('shows no misalignment on Qwen3-32B'). The baseline should be base Qwen3-32B, which is 0% on these prompts (Fig 9). The V7 link stands only as dataset/coherence dependence, which the authors attribute to incoherence.
